headline: Ten days: views 11,650→17,289 (+48%), subs 23→24 (+1). The shorts machine is fully working — four clips over 700 views this cycle (Make me a millionaire 1,214; baby egg allergy 1,148; dice rolls 940; Claude don't cut this out 729), all personality one-liners, while every concept clip flopped (NSA 75, freestyle 19, CLOSE IT 15) — but it converted almost nothing: one subscriber all cycle, zero subs from either new episode. The two big experiment reads: Ep 8's first-week CTR came in at 1.78% (2.6× Ep 7's 0.68%, below Ep 6's 3.24% — launch packaging mildly positive), and Ep 9 earned the channel's biggest first-week audition ever (2,527 impressions) but converted at just 1.23% — and it spent launch-day peak hours serving a truncated title variant ('…Catastrop') locked in Test & Compare (Jackson fixed it in Studio same day), a launch-day packaging failure of exactly the kind the gate exists to prevent. Ep 9's body is the best on the channel (16.5% avg view, 13.7% held flat from 40–80%, 9.8% at the end) but its open is the worst (−60.8pp by 1:41). Fix the first 90 seconds and the packaging gate, and the format is proven.

production.title: Launch-day packaging gate: Ep 8 passed (mildly), Ep 9 fumbled it — a Test & Compare variant shipped with a truncated title
production.evidence: Ep 8 first-week CTR (the number last review flagged as most important): 1.78% on 1,513 impressions — 2.6× Ep 7's 0.68%, still below Ep 6's 3.24%. Ep 9 drew 2,527 first-week impressions, the largest episode audition the channel has ever gotten (Ep 5: 1,712, Ep 8: 1,513), and converted at 1.23% — and per segment-times.md it went live 8/6 with the title variant 'Do Everything Right, Lose Everything: The Coldcard Catastrop' (missing 'he'), unfixable via API while Test & Compare held it. The API now returns the clean 'An AI Found the Bug. Then It Found Everyone's Bitcoin.' so a variant swap happened, but the broken variant was serving during the days that matter (95% of impressions land in the first 7 days).
production.recommendation: Extend the launch gate: proofread every Test & Compare variant BEFORE publish (the truncation was an input error, not a display limit), and don't start a title experiment on launch day unless all variants are verified. Ep 10 is the next clean test — target Ep 6's 3.24%.
production.status_note: Ep 8 = first clean launch test, positive. Ep 9 = gate violated by the truncated variant; Jackson fixed it in Studio same day (8/6), but it served during peak audition hours. Whether custom thumbnails were live at launch for either is still unverified.

production.title: Shorts→subscriber conversion is now THE channel problem: +5,639 views bought 1 subscriber
production.evidence: SHORTS traffic this window: 14,275 views / 885 watch-minutes (up ~3,828 views this cycle). Channel subs: +1 in 10 days. Both new episodes report subs_gained = 0. Meanwhile SUBSCRIBER traffic produced 1,522 watch-minutes off just 579 views — a subscriber is worth ~26× the watch-time of a shorts view. RELATED_VIDEO (the wired funnel) moved 97→130 views and 254→415 watch-minutes — real but tiny against 14k shorts views. Even with the funnel wired, the 1,214-view and 1,148-view shorts converted zero measurable subs.
production.recommendation: The wiring is done (Jackson runs the Ep 9 pinned comments as each short goes public); the question is now whether the funnel CAN convert at this shorts/episode affinity, or whether the shorts audience is just a different audience. Next pull: judge by RELATED_VIDEO (baseline 130 / 415) and subs. If it's still ~flat, the experiment shifts to clip choice — pull clips that tease an episode ARC (cliffhanger into the ?t= link) instead of self-contained punchlines.
production.status_note: Ep 9 funnel checklist done by Jackson 8/6 (pinned comments land as each short goes public — Studio-manual, don't re-report as pending). Ep 8's batch unconfirmed. 5 Ep 9 clips still scheduled-private through 8/13.

production.title: The opening leak moved INSIDE the cold open — Ep 9 loses half its audience mid-teaser, before the welcome even starts
production.evidence: Ep 9 opens hotter than anything prior (96.1% watching at 0:33, vs Ep 8's 74.1%) then sheds −51.0pp between 0:33 and 1:07 — entirely inside the 0:00–1:34 cold open — and another −9.8pp by 1:41. Total 0:33→1:41 loss: −60.8pp, the worst on the channel (Ep 6: −26.9pp; caveat: n=51 views, noisy). Ep 8: −38.9pp at 0:31→1:02, same shape. The seam-drop theory is dead: viewers aren't bailing at the welcome handoff, they're bailing when the teaser overstays.
production.recommendation: Cap the cold open at ~60 seconds. Ep 9's ran 94s. The hook lands (96% at 0:33) — get to the marquee before it decays. Pair with the recording-side welcome trim.

production.title: Clip selection: personality one-liners beat concept clips by 10–80×, again, with the biggest sample yet
production.evidence: This cycle's shorts: Make me a millionaire 1,214 / baby egg allergy 1,148 / dice rolls 940 / Claude don't cut this out 729 / commit 'runs' 323 vs concept or solo picks: NSA 75, My agent only buys Ripple 26, freestyle 19, CLOSE IT 15. Same pattern as Ep 6/7 cycles but at 5× the volume. Views track the human moment, not the topic.
production.recommendation: Already house style (personality/one-liner picks over concepts) — this is the confirmation data. When a batch needs a 9th clip, cut a second personality beat before a second concept.

production.title: Re-upload the Ep 2 clip as a new asset (carried)
production.evidence: Unchanged: 8,840 lifetime impressions at 0.42% CTR, now aged out to ~0/day. The re-audition experiment hasn't been run.
production.recommendation: Re-cut as a NEW upload with a hook title + thumbnail; it tests whether a fresh audition can be won with proven-demand content. Low effort, slot it behind the Ep 9 clip queue (after 8/13).

recording.title: Story-driven explainers hold; debate blocks leak — the 8-minute cap is really a stakes cap
recording.evidence: Ep 9's Coldcard block (5:16–17:30, ~12 min, Tyler owned the device) held 19.6–21.6% almost perfectly flat from 5:36 to 16:50 — the longest flat stretch on any episode, despite breaking the 8-minute cap. Ep 8's 'who gets the dangerous model' debate (8:33–18:34) dropped −5.6pp right at 8:22 as it started and stayed low. The differentiator isn't minutes, it's a host with skin in the game telling a story vs hosts arguing an abstraction.
recording.recommendation: Keep the cap for abstract/debate segments, but a personal-stakes narrative can run 12+ minutes. Slate rule: every explainer needs an owner with a story ('Tyler owned the exact device'), or it gets capped at 8 and paired with a live bit.

recording.title: Ep 8's final block bled out — don't park agentic commerce (or any standing topic) in the last 20%
recording.evidence: Ep 8 at 80–83% (41:50–43:24, inside 'Agentic commerce, finally' 38:47 + 'standards war' 45:38): vs_typical collapses to 0.07–0.05 and watch drops −7.4pp — the worst relative performance of any segment on either new episode. Contrast Ep 9's final stretch (frontier pissing contest → book-scanning → distillation): 13.7% held flat from 39:17 to 44:54 and 9.8% still present at the end.
recording.recommendation: Agentic commerce is on every slate (standing topic) — schedule it mid-show where Ep 9 put its strongest material, and end on the live/personal beat instead.

recording.title: Check-in placement fix VERIFIED on Ep 8 — keep it mid-show
recording.evidence: Last review's test: Ep 8 moved check-in to 18:34. Result: no crater — retention actually rises through that region (13.0% at 15:41 → 14.8% at 20:55), and the old 1:50–2:27 danger zone shows only the baseline opening decay (−5.6pp), no distinct check-in cliff like Ep 5's −9.1pp.
recording.recommendation: Locked in: check-in lives mid-show as a palate cleanser, never in the top 10 minutes. This item retires next review if Ep 9/10 don't contradict it.

recording.title: Don't ship a solo episode as the main feed item (standing)
recording.evidence: Unchanged since 7/31: Ep 7 (solo) remains worst on every axis — 0.68% CTR, 6.8% avg view, −56.7pp opening. No new solo episodes since; the two full-panel episodes since both beat it on every measure.
recording.recommendation: When hosts are out, ship a clip package or bring a guest.
